NoteTexAccessor::math_blocks¶

Back to Note TeX Accessor API Reference

Signature¶

TokenBatch NoteTexAccessor::math_blocks(std::int64_t max_count) const

Extract One Source-Ordered Stream Of Math Regions¶

math_blocks() extracts complete math regions written with any of TeX’s four common delimiter pairs: $...$, $$...$$, \(...\), and \[...\]. Every token retains its original delimiters, and inline and display regions remain interleaved in source order. This is the broad extractor to choose when the distinction between inline and display layout should not split the inventory.

max_count controls each receiver cell independently. -1 means unlimited, 0 returns an empty range for every cell without scanning for matches, and a positive value retains at most that many first regions from each cell. Values below -1 are invalid and are rejected before extraction.

Single-dollar regions cannot cross a physical newline. Escaped dollars do not open or close a region, and $$ is recognized before $ so a display fragment is never split into empty inline fragments. Backslash-delimited forms close at the next unescaped matching delimiter. An unmatched opener contributes no token. The scan is lexical: it neither executes TeX nor interprets comments, macro expansion, or environment semantics.

The returned TokenBatch stores flat Text tokens() plus Int64 offsets(). For receiver cell i, [offsets[i], offsets[i + 1]) is its source-ordered range. Limiting one cell never consumes another cell’s allowance. The flat token Note therefore remains compact even when a higher-rank receiver has very uneven match counts. Undefined input returns undefined tokens and offsets [0]; defined non-Text input is rejected.

Without a zero cap, runtime is linear in the visited source bytes plus copied token bytes. A positive cap permits the scanner to stop matching a lane as soon as that lane reaches its allowance. Returned strings are owned by the result.

Option Contract¶

max_count

Meaning

Scope

-1

Retain every complete region

Per cell

0

Retain no regions

Per cell

Positive

Retain the first max_count regions

Per cell

Below -1

Reject the call

Whole call

Example 1: Extract Every Delimiter Form¶

const auto source = pluss::make_note(
    std::vector<std::string>{
        R"(price \$5; $x+\$y$ then $$display$$ and \(z\))",
        "\\[block\\] and $line\nbreak$", R"(\(unfinished)", "plain"},
    std::array<std::int64_t, 2>{2, 2});
const auto all = source.tex().math_blocks(-1);

std::cout << all.tokens() << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[4], dim=1, numel=4, encoding=utf8)
["$x+\\$y$", "$$display$$", "\\(z\\)", "\\[block\\]"]

The escaped dollar remains inside its inline region. The newline-spanning single-dollar candidate and unmatched parenthesized opener are absent.

Example 2: Recover Higher-Rank Lane Ownership¶

std::cout << "offsets=[";
const auto offsets = all.offsets().integers();
for (std::size_t i = 0; i < offsets.size(); ++i)
  std::cout << (i ? ", " : "") << offsets[i];
std::cout << "]\n";

Output¶

offsets=[0, 3, 4, 4, 4]

The first matrix cell owns three regions, the second owns one, and the final two own none.

Example 3: Apply A Per-Cell Limit¶

const auto first = source.tex().math_blocks(1);
std::cout << first.tokens() << '\n';

std::cout << "offsets=[";
const auto offsets = first.offsets().integers();
for (std::size_t i = 0; i < offsets.size(); ++i)
  std::cout << (i ? ", " : "") << offsets[i];
std::cout << "]\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[2], dim=1, numel=2, encoding=utf8)
["$x+\\$y$", "\\[block\\]"]
offsets=[0, 1, 2, 2, 2]

Each of the first two cells receives its own allowance of one token.

Example 4: Request No Regions¶

const auto none = source.tex().math_blocks(0);
std::cout << none.tokens() << '\n';

std::cout << "offsets=[";
const auto offsets = none.offsets().integers();
for (std::size_t i = 0; i < offsets.size(); ++i)
  std::cout << (i ? ", " : "") << offsets[i];
std::cout << "]\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[0], dim=1, numel=0, encoding=utf8)
[]
offsets=[0, 0, 0, 0, 0]

An empty request still retains one boundary for every source lane plus the final boundary.

Example 5: Reject An Invalid Limit¶

try {
  (void)source.tex().math_blocks(-2);
} catch (const pluss::Error&) {
  std::cout << "math_blocks(-2): rejected\n";
}

Output¶

math_blocks(-2): rejected

Example 6: Undefined And Invalid Input¶

const auto absent = pluss::Note::undefined().tex().math_blocks(-1);
std::cout << std::boolalpha << absent.tokens().defined() << " offsets=["
          << absent.offsets().integers()[0] << "]\n";
try {
  (void)pluss::note::make(std::vector<std::int64_t>{1, 2})
      .tex().math_blocks(-1);
} catch (const pluss::Error&) {
  std::cout << "math blocks Int64: rejected\n";
}

Output¶

false offsets=[0]
math blocks Int64: rejected
